title: Why MCP exists
intro: Models are only as good as the context given to them — and before MCP, giving it to them meant custom glue everywhere.

steps.title: The analogy that explains everything
steps.body:
**REST** standardized how web apps talk to backends. **LSP** standardized how IDEs talk to language tools. **MCP** standardizes how AI applications talk to external systems.

> [!key] MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how your LLM applications connect to and work with your tools & data sources.

steps.title: M×N → M+N
steps.body:
**Without MCP**: AI App 1, 2 and 3 each build custom implementations — custom prompt logic, custom tool calls, custom data access — for every data source. M apps × N sources = M×N integrations.

**With MCP**: one MCP-compatible app connects to a Data-Store server, a CRM server, a version-control server through the same protocol — and the same Google Drive server serves an AI assistant, an AI agent, and an IDE, unchanged. M + N.

steps.title: Host, client, server
steps.body: Three roles carry the whole protocol:

points.label: Host
points.note: LLM applications that want to access data through MCP — Claude Desktop, IDEs, AI agents.

points.label: Client
points.note: Inside the host, maintaining a 1:1 connection with one server over the MCP protocol.

points.label: Server
points.note: A lightweight program exposing specific capabilities — tools, resources, prompt templates.

steps.title: Who wins, and the FAQ
steps.body:
- **App developers**: connect to any server with zero additional work.
- **Tool/API developers**: build a server once, adopted everywhere (3,000+ community servers and counting).
- **Users**: apps with extensive capabilities. **Enterprises**: separation of concerns between AI teams.

> [!tip] "Isn't this just tool use?" — With direct API calls you author schemas and functions yourself, every time. **An MCP server ships them already defined** — often by the service provider itself.

recap:
**MCP = REST/LSP for AI apps: one protocol, not M×N glue.**

- Host (wants context) → client (1:1 protocol session) → server (capabilities).
- Servers are reusable across every MCP-compatible app.
- The value: schemas + functions defined once, by whoever knows the service best.
- Ecosystem: thousands of servers, hosts from IDEs to agents.
